reason: The sources provide well-supported facts across multiple independent sites regarding Voyager 1's launch, mission, flybys, interstellar transition, and equipment.
story: In September 1977, NASA launched Voyager 1 from Cape Canaveral aboard a Titan rocket, embarking on a grand tour of the outer planets. Built and operated by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the spacecraft made groundbreaking flybys of Jupiter and Saturn, discovering active volcanoes on the moon Io and examining Saturn's giant moon Titan. Powered by plutonium thermoelectric generators, the probe continued driving outward past the planets. In August 2012, Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space, officially becoming the most distant human-made object in history. To keep its high-gain antenna locked onto Earth via the Deep Space Network, engineers successfully fired backup thrusters that had slept unused for decades. Led by project scientist Ed Stone, the craft carries a 12-inch Golden Record compiled by Carl Sagan and Timothy Ferris, designed to carry the sounds and images of Earth through the galaxy forever.
angle: Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to cross into interstellar space, firing backup thrusters dormant for decades to keep transmitting from the void.

claims.claim: Voyager 1 was launched after its twin probe, Voyager 2.
Voyager 1 was launched aboard a Titan III rocket.
NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory built and operates the Voyager 1 spacecraft.
Voyager 1 completed a close flyby of Jupiter.
Voyager 1 completed a close flyby of Saturn.
Voyager 1 was targeted to conduct a close flyby of Saturn's largest moon, Titan.
Voyager 1 discovered active volcanoes on Jupiter's moon Io.
Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause and entered interstellar space in August 2012.
Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object from Earth.
Voyager 1 carries a 12-inch golden record containing sounds and images from Earth.
Carl Sagan led the committee that created the Voyager Golden Record.
Timothy Ferris was part of the team that produced the Voyager Golden Record.
Edward Stone served as the project scientist for the Voyager mission.
Voyager 1 is powered by radioisotope thermoelectric generators fueled by plutonium.
Engineers successfully fired Voyager 1's backup trajectory correction thrusters after decades of disuse.
Voyager 1 communicates with Earth using NASA's Deep Space Network.
Voyager 1 carries a plasma wave instrument to detect oscillations in space.

disputed: The exact timing and location of Voyager 1's crossing of the termination shock was debated among scientists (some claiming late 2003 and others late 2004) because its primary solar-wind detector stopped functioning in 1990; script should attribute or frame as inferred from indirect particle data.

Whether crossing the heliopause means leaving the Solar System entirely is disputed semantically, as the Oort cloud extends far beyond; script should clarify it entered interstellar space without leaving the full gravitational boundary of the Oort cloud.
